gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-warang-ci: Ancient and powerful, Nordic strokes its cramped, monoweight letters with wide gaps between them. Noto Sans Warang Citi is the one that opens up, giving words solid, clean blocks to settle into.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-yi: Nordic traces every letter as a single constant-width outline, spaced like brush dabs far apart. Noto Sans Yi follows with a deep lowercase midsection and hooked rounds left unsealed, so the two feel like carved stone beside quick handwriting.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar: Chunky, bent-cable letters up top. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square gives the pair its best quality: a soaring x-height and wide gaps that stay crisp even at tiny sizes, against Nordic's closed, ancient shapes.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-traditional-nu: Noto Traditional Nushu writes with a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls shut, and its bowls fill the line. Noto Traditional Nushu would feel approachable over a long page, a gentle counterweight to Nordic's cramped, powerful headings.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-numans: Numans stretches its swollen lowercase out with generous tracking, and its s hangs its ends far from the spine. Nordic's closed, ancient capitals are the sharp counterpoint.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-onest: Onest keeps its ascenders short above big bowls and its line thickness gently uniform, with no ink pooling in the turns. Nordic's closed, ancient letters sit against it.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-open-sans: Open Sans reads smoothly, with bulky lowercase and no clogged curves anywhere. Open Sans would swamp Nordic if enlarged, and Nordic would lose its cramped, leaf-fold character if the heading shrank too small.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-orienta: Ancient, heavy-handed, and brushed with space: that's Nordic, with a w drawn without thick or thin strokes. Orienta breathes like a hollow reed, and its lowercase nearly matches its capitals, so a size close to the heading's would hold up.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-oxygen: Oxygen reads with curves that never close back on themselves. Its lowercase nearly matches the capitals, so a long page would feel clean and contemporary beside Nordic's cramped, ancient headings.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-parkinsans: Nordic is powerful and ancient, spacing its monoweight letters like brush dabs far apart. And Parkinsans is the one that stays crisp when shrunk, its wide-mouthed lowercase rising close to the capitals.
